parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, border friction, facility ban, police targeting, custody-placement rule, or anti-trans violence is documented. The formal climate is strongly protective — gender recognition, equality protection, and a conversion-therapy ban — but these are largely resident-facing climate signals rather than direct visitor shields. Visitor-specific evidence is thin: no documented acceptance in hotels/transport, no border-marker practice, unresolved hate-crime bill status, and no prison placement finding. In a well-documented jurisdiction, silence is moderately positive, but it does not establish functioning visitor-facing protection. Open questions and resident-only gaps are not exposures, so this is not high risk; the absence of demonstrated visitor protections keeps it below the low-risk band.
